Cash back is in the form of electronic awards issued in $20 increments that are used at checkout at BJ’s and expire 6 months from the date issued. we need data points on the us bank business edge if you cna sign up multiple au and still get the 200 dollars after you finish the application? which credit union does it pull from? and if anyone tried adding au number 11 and 12 etc and you were still able to get the 200 dolar credit! and what about using childrens under 18 ssn ? or a made up ssn like amex for the first 60 days?

Downsides: Any new card counts against 5/24 Chase. 6/24 Barclays. It’s usually better to seek signup bonuses ($200+ for $500-1K spend, or higher, for example) rather than long term rewards that pay out twenty-forty-whatever per year. And pre-approved offers still come with a hard inquiry usually, so all that means is you are more likely to be approved.

Most everyone has a flat 2% card… so anything at or less isn’t worth the keystrokes.

6 months is a short expiration. You had better be able to get some good use of the card so you can collect the rewards.

But, if you like BJ’s and use it…. enjoy. If you are spending just to spend, or going on occasional sprees or once a year trips, it’s not worth your time.

My thought was pre-approved meant no hard pull, thus no 5/24. That’s the only reason I considered getting the card as it may prove MS useful and the 6 months is not an issue. Now I see from a DoC post that there is a hard pull. “Pre-approved” is deceptive. Thanks for helping out.
Hard pulls are completely separate from 5/24. 5/24 checks actual credit cards on your account, all personal cards will show up regardless of if a hard pull was done to check your credit.

Right, as I said in my post, I was operating under a mis-understanding and am now better informed. But thanks for the reply. That “pre-approved” language probably reels in a few fish. I think it’s deceptive.

Sorry, I see you understand now, your previous post still seemed to equate 5/24 count with hard pulls, just wanted to make sure things were clear. Glad you stayed away from the offer.

I don’t think its deceptive to say you’re pre-approved. They’re happy to give you the card. Just because you are pre-approved doesn’t mean you should apply.

Why I think it is deceptive is that there is essentially no difference between “pre-qualified” and “pre-approved”. The former is more honest as any schmo is qualified to apply. “Pre-approval” is designed to infer more status when it does not actually deliver it.

Anybody has an idea on how strict the 90 days period is? I have a spending 5000$ within 90 days to get 500$ offer, and I just found one transaction is posted 3 days late which made the spending exceed 2 days, so I met the bonus requirement in 92 days instead of 90 days. Is it possible to get the bonus in this case? It is really a bummer. Lesson: do not assume the credit card transaction will post the next day.
No, only AUs added when you sign up getting the bonus.

@arch You’re still misunderstanding. It doesn’t matter whether there is a hard pull or not. Your credit report will show the new credit account, and Chase 5/24 rule counts newly opened lines of credit, not pulls. (That can be good — being declined for a card does not create a strike against 5/24)

Many banks internally track on an extended deadline to avoid disqualifying bonuses on a technicality, since unhappy customers are worse than paying out the bonus. (At least concerning customers who actually are putting the spend on their new card)

However not all banks do. If you’re worried, I recommend keeping the receipt that shows the actual transaction date.
